_comment: AOS Sprint 9 — Reverse Job Hunt Engine. Every table here is a deterministic lookup keyed by demand-intelligence's own five category keys, or by Buying Readiness Band, or by this engine's own new six-value entry-point vocabulary. Does not modify demand_engine.py, ingest.py or account_intelligence_engine.py's scoring in any way; every number here is either read directly from an upstream employee's own already-computed field, or a small, clearly-labelled new heuristic. Edit this file to retune wording/mappings — no code change needed.

categoryAiMaturityLabel._note: Credited, verbatim copy of account-intelligence/runtime/config/account-intelligence-config.json's own categoryAiMaturityLabel table — the same deterministic label, reused here so both employees describe the same underlying fact identically rather than risk drifting apart.

categoryGovernanceMaturityLabel._note: A distinct question from AI maturity: how developed is this organisation's AI GOVERNANCE specifically, not its AI adoption. New in Sprint 9 — Account Intelligence (Sprint 8) only asked about AI maturity, not governance maturity separately.
categoryGovernanceMaturityLabel.ai_adoption: Ad hoc / informal — no governance signal on record yet, only deployment
categoryGovernanceMaturityLabel.governance_trigger: Developing — a governance function is being stood up, not yet mature
categoryGovernanceMaturityLabel.funding_trigger: Initial — not yet formalised, funding is outpacing governance
categoryGovernanceMaturityLabel.regulatory_trigger: Developing, compliance-driven — maturity is being built specifically to meet a named obligation
categoryGovernanceMaturityLabel.failure_trigger: Immature / reactive — a gap already caused a real incident

categoryPursuitReason._note: Section 1 'why pursue' — one factual clause per matched category, combined across all matched categories.
categoryPursuitReason.ai_adoption: it is already deploying AI at scale, which reliably outpaces informal governance
categoryPursuitReason.governance_trigger: it is actively building a formal AI governance function right now, the exact window where an external advisor's input has the most influence
categoryPursuitReason.funding_trigger: newly-raised capital is about to fund AI expansion faster than internal oversight can track
categoryPursuitReason.regulatory_trigger: it has a named external regulatory or compliance obligation on record, which creates a hard deadline rather than a discretionary one
categoryPursuitReason.failure_trigger: a public AI-related incident has already occurred, which is the single strongest, most time-sensitive pursuit trigger this engine tracks

categoryRelevanceReason._note: Section 3 'why AI for U&I is relevant' — pairs each category with the specific practice-area relevance, distinct from Section 1's pursuit urgency.
categoryRelevanceReason.ai_adoption: AI for U&I's ADGL methodology exists specifically for organisations at this deployment stage
categoryRelevanceReason.governance_trigger: AI for U&I's AI Governance Operating Model and Executive Workshop are built for exactly this stand-up moment
categoryRelevanceReason.funding_trigger: an AI Governance Operating Model established now is materially cheaper than retrofitting one after scaling
categoryRelevanceReason.regulatory_trigger: AI for U&I's AI Policy & Control Framework and Third-Party Risk Review map directly to named regulatory obligations
categoryRelevanceReason.failure_trigger: AI for U&I's AI Risk Assessment and Policy & Control Framework are built for post-incident remediation and evidencing corrective action

entryPoint._note: Section 6 — six-value vocabulary. Precedence, top to bottom: an existing CRM relationship always wins (a warm path beats any cold one); otherwise low confidence in the underlying signal always means the lightest-touch option regardless of band; otherwise Buying Readiness Band plus whether an urgent category (governance/regulatory/failure trigger) is present decides the rest. Every value below is genuinely reachable — see tests/test_reverse_job_hunt_engine.py's EntryPointTests.

timelineByBand._note: Section 8 'recommended timeline' — when to START outreach, not how long the deal will take to close (that is a different question; see opportunity_scorecard-style estimatedSalesCycle in account-intelligence, which this engine deliberately does not duplicate).

firstTouchTemplateByEntryPoint._note: Section 9 'recommended first touch' — one concrete, low-risk next action per entry point, parameterised only by {organisation} and {categoryLabel} (the organisation's own strongest matched category label) — never a drafted sales pitch.
firstTouchTemplateByEntryPoint.LinkedIn relationship: Send a LinkedIn connection request to a relevant stakeholder at {organisation}, referencing their public {categoryLabel} activity — no ask, just visibility.
firstTouchTemplateByEntryPoint.Warm introduction: Ask the existing CRM contact/recruiter for {organisation} for a direct introduction to the relevant stakeholder.
firstTouchTemplateByEntryPoint.Conference: Identify a governance/AI-risk conference or event {organisation}'s stakeholders are likely to attend, and plan an in-person introduction there.
firstTouchTemplateByEntryPoint.Executive briefing: Offer a short, no-obligation executive briefing on the governance implications of {organisation}'s {categoryLabel} activity.
firstTouchTemplateByEntryPoint.Discovery workshop: Propose a structured discovery workshop to scope {organisation}'s governance gap directly.
firstTouchTemplateByEntryPoint.Fractional advisory: Propose a fractional advisory conversation — {organisation}'s signal strength and category warrant discussing an ongoing arrangement, not just a one-off engagement.

ninetyDaySequenceByEntryPoint._note: Section 10 — a three-phase, 90-day sequence per entry point. Deliberately conditional in phrasing ("if engaged... if not...") since this engine has no response-tracking data to branch on deterministically; a human decides which branch applies as it unfolds.
LinkedIn relationship: Days 1-30: Send the connection request (Section 9); if accepted, engage lightly with their public posts — no direct ask.

Days 31-60: If engagement continues, share one relevant AI for U&I resource (Section 8 of the Account Intelligence brief, if one exists); if no response, move to Conference as a second, lower-pressure channel.
Days 61-90: If a real conversation has started, propose a short executive briefing; if not, keep the connection warm and re-evaluate at the next signal.
Warm introduction: Days 1-30: Request the introduction (Section 9); follow up once if no response within two weeks.
Days 31-60: Once introduced, offer a short, no-obligation conversation about their current governance approach.
Days 61-90: If the conversation confirmed genuine need, propose a discovery workshop; if not yet, stay in light touch via the referring contact.
Conference: Days 1-30: Identify the specific event and confirm attendance plans; request a brief introduction on-site if a mutual contact exists.
Days 31-60: Follow up after the event referencing the specific conversation, not a generic pitch.
Days 61-90: If interest was genuine, propose an executive briefing; if not, keep on the LinkedIn relationship track instead.
Executive briefing: Days 1-30: Offer the briefing directly (Section 9); confirm a date within the first two weeks if accepted.
Days 31-60: Deliver the briefing; follow up within a week with the specific governance risks discussed.
Days 61-90: If the briefing lands well, propose a discovery workshop or fractional advisory conversation; if not, de-prioritise to Monitor.
Discovery workshop: Days 1-30: Propose the workshop directly (Section 9), with a concrete agenda scoped to their strongest matched category.
Days 31-60: Run the workshop; document findings and a recommended next step.
Days 61-90: Convert workshop findings into a formal proposal if warranted; if not ready, schedule a check-in at day 90.
Fractional advisory: Days 1-30: Propose the fractional advisory conversation directly (Section 9), framed around their most urgent matched category.
Days 31-60: If there is interest, scope a fractional engagement structure and cadence.
Days 61-90: Finalise terms if genuinely ready; otherwise fall back to a discovery workshop as a lower-commitment alternative.

consultingPotentialScaleThresholds._note: Section 2 fallback only — used when no real opportunity-schema.json record exists for this organisation yet. Same regex convention demand_engine.py's own _extract_scale_number() already uses (first number in the profile's scale text), reimplemented locally rather than imported, keeping this employee's runtime self-contained like every other AOS employee.
consultingPotentialScaleThresholds.veryLargeLabel: High (10 — large-scale deployment implies a substantial governance programme)
consultingPotentialScaleThresholds.unclearLabel: Unclear — insufficient scale data (3, conservative default)
